title: PROVISIONAL ESTIMATES OF WHOLESALE PRICE INDEX, OUTPUT PRODUCER PRICE INDEX, AND TRIAL INPUT PRODUCER PRICE INDEX FOR THE MONTH OF JULY 2026, AND FINAL INDEX FOR THE MONTH OF MAY 2026
subtitle: Provisional Estimates of Wholesale Price Index (Base Year 2022-23) for the month of July 2026
body_text:
Key highlights of WPI (Base Year 2022-23) for July 2026
All India Wholesale Price Index (WPI) inflation for July 2026 is 9.78 per cent on year-on-year (YoY) basis, compared to 9.87 per cent in June 2026. The index for All Commodities for July 2026 stands at 110.0, whereas it was 110.2 in June 2026. YoY inflation rates for major groups, namely, Primary Articles, Fuel and Power, and Manufactured Products are 8.52 per cent, 20.05 per cent, and 8.29 per cent, respectively in July 2026, compared to 7.0 per cent, 27.41 per cent, and 7.48 per cent, respectively in June 2026. The indices for Primary Articles, Fuel and Power, and Manufactured Products are 117.2, 105.4, and 108.4, respectively, in July 2026, whereas they were 116.1, 111.1, and 107.8, respectively, in June 2026. Across groups, ‘Mineral Oils (containing Petroleum Products) ’, ‘Food Articles’, ‘Manufacture of Basic Metals’, ‘Non-Food Articles’, ‘Manufacture of Food Products’, and ‘Manufacture of Chemicals and Chemical Products’ have been major drivers of WPI inflation in July 2026. WPI Food Index (weight=24.99 per cent): The Food Index consists of ‘Food Articles’ from Primary Articles major group, and ‘Manufacture of Food Products’ from Manufactured Products major group. It observed a YoY inflation of 6.65 per cent in July 2026, compared to 6.14 per cent in June 2026. Monthly indices and Inflation Rate (in per cent) for All commodities and Major Groups, along with major group-wise contribution for the past months are presented in the charts below.
Chart 1: WPI Index and Inflation Rate for All Commodities Chart 2: WPI Index of Major Groups Chart 3: Inflation Rate across Major Groups Chart 4: Major Group-Wise contribution to Inflation The final index for the month of May 2026 has been revised from 109.9 (Provisional estimate) to 110.1. Accordingly, WPI inflation has been revised from 9.68 per cent, as per provisional estimate to 9.88 per cent as per the final estimate. The Final Estimate of WPI (Base Year 2022-23) for the month of May 2026 has been compiled with a weighted response rate of 98.14 per cent. The Provisional Estimate of WPI (Base Year 2022-23) for the month of July 2026 has been compiled with a weighted response rate of 78.55 per cent. Wholesale Price Index and Year-on-Year (YoY) Inflation Rate for All Commodities, Major Groups, and Groups for the last six months is given at Annexure-I and II respectively. Cumulative WPI for All Commodities, Major Groups, and Groups from April to July for FY 2023-24, FY 2024-25, FY 2025-26, and FY 2026-27 is given at Annexure-III. Cumulative YoY Inflation Rate for All Commodities, Major Groups, and Groups from April to July for FY 2024-25, FY 2025-26, and FY 2026-27 is given at Annexure- IV. Item-wise data pertaining to WPI (Base Year 2022-23) series from April 2023 to July 2026 is available at (https://eaindustry.nic.in/download_data_2223.asp ). Provisional indices of WPI, OPPI, and trial IPPI for a reference month are released on the 14 th of the following month (if it is a working day, else on next working day). Accordingly, release of WPI, Output PPI, and trial Input PPI for the month of August 2026 will be on Monday, 14 th September 2026.

enrichment.summary: The Ministry of Commerce & Industry released provisional Wholesale Price Index (WPI, Base Year 2022-23) data for July 2026, showing WPI inflation at 9.78% year-on-year, marginally down from 9.87% in June 2026. Primary Articles inflation rose to 8.52%, while Fuel and Power inflation fell sharply to 20.05% from 27.41%, and Manufactured Products inflation rose to 8.29%. The Food Index recorded 6.65% YoY inflation, and the final WPI for May 2026 was revised upward from 9.68% (provisional) to 9.88%.
enrichment.context:
The Wholesale Price Index measures the average change in prices of goods at the wholesale/producer level and is released monthly by the Office of the Economic Adviser under the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT). It differs from the Consumer Price Index (CPI), which captures retail-level prices faced by consumers and is used by the RBI for inflation targeting under its flexible inflation targeting framework (4% +/- 2% band based on CPI, not WPI). WPI is closely watched as a leading indicator of pipeline price pressures that may eventually pass through to retail prices, and it also feeds into the GDP deflator used for calculating real GDP growth.

India moved to WPI Base Year 2022-23 relatively recently (from the earlier 2011-12 base), reflecting revised weights for commodity groups such as Primary Articles, Fuel and Power, and Manufactured Products. The release also introduces newer disaggregated indices—the Output Producer Price Index (OPPI) and a trial Input Producer Price Index (IPPI)—which are experimental national statistical initiatives aimed at eventually developing a full Producer Price Index (PPI) system, aligning India's price statistics architecture more closely with international best practices recommended by the IMF and UN Statistics Division. The elevated WPI figures here, driven substantially by mineral oils, food articles, and basic metals, are relevant to macroeconomic policy discussions on inflation, monetary policy transmission, and fiscal management of subsidies (e.g., LPG, fertiliser) sensitive to wholesale fuel and commodity price movements.

prelims_questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Wholesale Price Index (WPI) in India:
1. It is released monthly by the Office of the Economic Adviser, DPIIT.
2. The Reserve Bank of India uses WPI as the primary index for its flexible inflation targeting framework.
3. The current base year for WPI is 2022-23.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
prelims_questions.explanation: WPI is released by the Office of the Economic Adviser under DPIIT (statement 1, correct) and uses base year 2022-23 as per this release (statement 3, correct). However, the RBI's flexible inflation targeting framework is based on CPI, not WPI (statement 2 is incorrect).

prelims_questions.question: In the WPI data released for July 2026, which major group recorded the highest year-on-year inflation rate?
prelims_questions.explanation: As per the release, Fuel and Power recorded the highest YoY inflation among major groups at 20.05% in July 2026, compared to 8.52% for Primary Articles, 8.29% for Manufactured Products, and 6.65% for the Food Index.

mains_questions.question: Distinguish between the Wholesale Price Index (WPI) and Consumer Price Index (CPI) in India. Discuss why divergence between the two indices matters for monetary policy formulation and subsidy management.

Examine the significance of developing a comprehensive Producer Price Index (PPI) system in India, referring to ongoing initiatives such as the Output PPI and trial Input PPI. How would this improve macroeconomic data governance?
mains_questions.gs_paper: GS Paper 3 - Economy: Statistics and Data Governance

study_notes.reason: The release is a monthly statistical bulletin: its value lies in specific index figures, base year, publishing authority and new index concepts (OPPI, IPPI) rather than in sustained analysis, though the fuel/food inflation divergence offers a modest analytical angle.

prelims.point: WPI Base Year is 2022-23 (revised from earlier 2011-12 base), released by Office of the Economic Adviser, DPIIT, Ministry of Commerce & Industry
prelims.why_important: UPSC frequently tests base years of key indices and the releasing authority; this is a recently changed base year likely to be probed.

prelims.point: WPI vs CPI: WPI measures wholesale/producer prices (DPIIT), CPI measures retail prices and is used by RBI for flexible inflation targeting (4% +/-2%)
prelims.why_important: A classic UPSC distinction-based question between two similarly named but differently used indices.

prelims.point: Output Producer Price Index (OPPI) and trial Input Producer Price Index (IPPI) are new experimental indices introduced alongside WPI, aimed at building a full Producer Price Index (PPI) system aligned with IMF/UN Statistics Division standards
prelims.why_important: A newly introduced statistical instrument is a natural target for a factual question on India's evolving price-statistics architecture.

prelims.point: WPI feeds into the GDP deflator used to calculate real GDP from nominal GDP
prelims.why_important: Connects a producer price index to national income accounting, a conceptual link UPSC could test.

mains.point: Sharp divergence between Fuel & Power inflation (still ~20%) and other groups signals continued pipeline price pressure from energy costs that could pass through to retail prices and affect subsidy burden on LPG/fertiliser
mains.analytical_use: Useful for a question on monetary-fiscal policy coordination or on challenges in managing subsidy costs amid volatile global commodity prices.

mains.point: Persistent gap between WPI (near 10%) and CPI trends highlights the difficulty of using WPI as a leading indicator for RBI's CPI-based inflation targeting
mains.analytical_use: Can be deployed in an answer on limitations of India's inflation-targeting framework or the WPI-CPI divergence puzzle.
